title: WAYNE COUNTY SHERIFF’S REPORT
full_story:
On Wednesday Wayne County Deputies conducted a traffic stop in Geff.

During the traffic stop the driver Dillon S. Hewkin, 33, of Geff attempted to obstruct his arrest by refusing to identify himself or provide identification.  It was determined it was Hewkin and he was placed under arrest for the following charges, Driving while license revoked, Obstructing Justice, and a Clay County Arrest Warrant.

On Friday Wayne County Deputies located Susan J. Grove, 46, of Fairfield at her residence and took her into custody for an active Wayne County Warrant.

During her arrest, responding deputies arrived on scene to assist the lone Deputy inside the residence.  At this time Shaun D. Carl began screaming at Deputies and locked the door so the back-up Deputies could not aid the lone Deputy inside the residence.  Carl refused commands to unlock the door and was arrested for obstructing justice.

title: RESTITUTION ORDER REVERSED
full_story:
Friday the Fifth District Appellate Court has reversed a restitution order in the case of the death of Stephanie Harrell.

On October 21st of 2024 Emily S Denning of Flora entered an open plea to the court and the state requested the maximum sentence, noting that with defendant’s previously served time, she would likely only be incarcerated for 60 days.  It also requested restitution for the victim’s children, James Harrell and Abra Howe, in the amount of $1,000 each because they had been in court, missed work and school, and had to pay for a funeral.  Dennings bond of $2,000 was split between the children.

Denning was originally charged with concealment of homicidal death with the intent to obstruct the prosecution of Phillip Blaine Henson.”

On appeal Denning argued that that the trial court’s award of restitution at her sentencing hearing was erroneous because the order failed to set out the method and manner of payment and the court failed to consider defendant’s ability to pay the restitution.  She further argued that insufficient evidence was presented to show that defendant’s conduct was proximately related to or caused the decedent’s death and the “lost wages” of the victim’s children.

The Fifth Appellate Court found that the Clay County court’s restitution order was erroneously entered without sufficient evidentiary support and remand the case back to the county for a new restitution hearing.

title: ALL AMERICAN BOY AND GIRL
full_story:

title: AREA FIREWORKS SHOWS
full_story:
Fireworks will be featured at area communities starting Thursday night.

The festivities begin Thursday in Fairfield with Freedom Fest at Southwest Park from 5 to 10 pm.  The event will feature inflatables, children’s games, a foam pit, putt-putt golf, food trucks and craft vendors, live music, and fireworks at dusk.  Country artist Noah Atwood is scheduled to perform.  Admission is free.

The Village of Cisne will kick off its Independence Day celebration on Friday, with an evening of food, live entertainment, and fireworks.  Food trucks will open at 5 pm in the back parking lot of Cisne High School.  Vendors scheduled to participate include Lil Buddies Snack Trailer, The Fair Lady, and Krazy Sweet Treats.  TrustBank will sponsor the first 100 snow cones for attendees.  The celebration will conclude with a fireworks display at dusk at the high school ball diamond.

title: ORCHARDVILLE SMALL TOWN LIFE WINNERS
full_story:

The Little All American Princess was Maddilyn Whipple, daughter of Ronnie and Nikki Whipple of Centralia.

title: BODY FOUND IN LAKE MATTOON
full_story:
Illinois State Police (ISP) Division of Criminal Investigations Zone 8 is seeking the public’s assistance identifying the remains of a man discovered in Lake Mattoon.

On Sunday evening, boaters observed part of a human arm in Lake Mattoon.  The Cumberland County Sheriff’s Office requested ISP adopt the investigation.  The arm has distinct tattoos and ISP is hoping this will help in identifying the man.

If anyone has any information regarding a man with tattoos matching the pictures, or has any other information which may be helpful, police ask that they contact ISP Zone 8 Investigations at 618-542-2400 or email [email protected].

title: CASEY MAN FOUND DEAD
full_story:
A Casey man missing for close to a week was found dead Saturday.

76-year-old Frank Mumford was found in his pickup truck.  Mumford was last seen on Sunday, June 21st in the Casey and Greenup area.  A plane was sent to fly the area Saturday.  Cumberland County Coroner Jennifer Phipps said during the flyover, a truck was spotted.  Phipps said a man identified as Mumford was found in the truck after floodwaters subsided.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
Some corn and soybean fields are progressing ahead of average pace with soybeans beginning to set pods before the Fourth of July.

USDA’s latest crop progress and condition report released Monday reported 8% of Illinois corn is silking, 3 percentage points ahead of the five-year average, and 17% of soybeans are blooming, 5 points ahead of average. Soybeans in the pod-setting stage reached 3%, compared to none at the same time last year and on average.

There were 2.7 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending June 28th.  Statewide, the average temperature was 70 degrees, 4.4 degrees below normal.  Precipitation averaged 2.41 inches, 1.34 inches above normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 2% very short, 5% short, 54% adequate, and 39% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 4% very short, 8% short, 62% adequate, and 26% surplus.

Corn silking reached 8%, compared to the 5-year average of 5%.  Corn condition was rated 3% very poor, 8% poor, 29% fair, 47% good, and 13% excellent.

Soybeans emerged reached 95%, equal to the 5-year average.  Soybeans blooming reached 17%, compared to the 5-year average of 13%.  Soybeans setting pods reached 3%, ahead of the 5-year average.  Soybean condition was rated 3% very poor, 9% poor, 33% fair, 43% good, and 12% excellent.

Winter wheat harvested reached 64%, compared to the 5-year average of 69%.  Winter wheat condition was rated 1% very poor, 5% poor, 19% fair, 59% good, and 16% excellent.

title: IDNR DIRECTOR TO DEPART AGENCY
full_story:
Governor JB Pritzker announced Friday the departure of Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) Director Natalie Phelps Finnie.  Having overseen a period of growth and reinvestment in the agency, Today is Finnie’s last day.

Finnie, of Hardin County was appointed IDNR director on January 23rd, of 2023.  Prior to that, she served as deputy director of the agency since August 2021.

During her tenure, Finnie launched impactful new programs and initiatives.  She created the “Everyone Belongs in Nature” campaign to reinforce that outdoor spaces are for everyone, no matter where they live or their background.  She also opened Illinois’ first state owned off highway vehicle trails at the Sahara Woods State Recreation Area in Saline County and expanded sustainability efforts by installing electric vehicle charging stations at state parks.

Renee Snow will serve as IDNR’s interim director beginning tomorrow.  She has worked at the department since 2014, most recently serving as general counsel.
